Scenario Name: Adding all six catalog products reaches maximal cart state
Error Log: TimeoutError: locator.click: Timeout 15000ms exceeded. Call log: - waiting for getByTestId('inventory-item').filter({ hasText: 'Test.allTheThings T-Shirt (Red)' }).getByRole('button', { name: /add to cart/i })
Probable Root Cause: Automation defect. The locator uses the product name 'Test.allTheThings T-Shirt (Red)', but the product name shown on saucedemo.com is 'Test.allTheThings() T-Shirt (Red)' (with parentheses). hasText does a substring match, so the filter never matches and the click waits the full 15s. The failure repeated on retry, which fits a deterministic data mismatch and not a flaky one. Other tests that add products by name pass.
Suggested Fix: Correct the product name constant to 'Test.allTheThings() T-Shirt (Red)', or match by a regex or data-test id such as add-to-cart-test.allthethings()-t-shirt-(red). Then re-run.

Scenario Name: Script/SQL-injection-style input in the shipping form is not executed
Error Log: Error: Unexpected console errors: Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 401 (Unauthorized); Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 401 (Unauthorized) | expect(received).toHaveLength(expected) Expected length: 0 Received length: 2
Probable Root Cause: Automation defect (over-strict assertion). The test asserts zero browser console errors, but the demo site always emits two 401 'Failed to load resource' console messages from its third-party telemetry or backend calls. These are unrelated to the injected input. No sign that the payload was executed, since the failing assertion is only the console-error count.
Suggested Fix: Filter known benign console noise (401 Failed to load resource) out of the console-error assertion, or assert only on script-execution signals such as dialogs or window flags. Compare against a baseline run with benign input to confirm the 401s occur there too.

Scenario Name: Direct URL navigation to checkout-complete.html without completing prior steps
Error Log: Error: expect(locator).not.toHaveText(expected) failed Locator: getByTestId('complete-header') Expected pattern: not /thank you for your order/i Received string: "Thank you for your order!"
Probable Root Cause: Application defect. After a direct visit to checkout-complete.html with no order placed, the app renders the 'Thank you for your order!' confirmation. There is no server or state guard on the page, so the confirmation can be reached without a cart or checkout. The locator resolved 13 times with the same value, so this is not a timing issue, and it repeated on retry.
Suggested Fix: File a defect: checkout-complete should redirect to the cart or inventory (or show an error) when no order was completed in the session. If this is accepted behavior of the demo site, change the test to document it as a known-issue baseline.

Error Log: TimeoutError: locator.click: Timeout 15000ms exceeded. Call log: - waiting for getByTestId('inventory-item').filter({ hasText: 'Sauce Labs Backpack' }).getByRole('button', { name: /add to cart/i })
Probable Root Cause: Probable automation defect, with some uncertainty. The 'Add to cart' button for Sauce Labs Backpack was never available. Likely causes are (a) cart state left over from the earlier user or step in the same browser session, so the button already reads 'Remove', or (b) problem_user's known broken inventory UI toggling button state incorrectly. The failure repeated on retry, so it is deterministic. The single-user problem_user and performance_glitch_user scenarios (SCN-27, SCN-28) pass, which points at the multi-user sequencing in this test and not the app.
Suggested Fix: Clear the cart, or use a fresh browser context, between the problem_user and performance_glitch_user segments. Log which user was active when the failure occurred. Make the helper tolerate a button already in the 'Remove' state, then re-run.

Scenario Name: Rapid double-click on Finish creates a single order
Error Log: Error: Expected a single navigation to the confirmation page expect(received).toBe(expected) // Object.is equality Expected: 1 Received: 2
Probable Root Cause: Undetermined: either an application defect or a flawed test measurement. Two navigations to the confirmation page were counted after a rapid double-click on Finish, which may mean the second click re-submitted the order (a duplicate-submission defect). It may also mean the test's navigation counter picks up a duplicate framenavigated or history event from a single order. The failure repeated on retry, so it is reproducible. There is not enough evidence in the report to tell the two apart.
Suggested Fix: Reproduce manually or with tracing: check whether Finish is still clickable after the first click and whether two distinct order or confirmation states result. If only one order is created, count completed orders (for example cart empty and one confirmation) and not raw navigation events. If a duplicate really occurs, file a defect to disable the button after the first click.
